basis: A repository thesis explicitly identifies the Harvard dissertation as the source of Ian Klaus's Forging Capitalism. Harvard independently lists the dissertation under Ian Klaus.

evidence.says: Gabriele Jancke's publications include Autobiographie als soziale Praxis (2002) and the 2004 report Bilanz und Perspektiven der Selbstzeugnisforschung.

basis: Freie Universität Berlin's publication list attributes the work on each key to the same Gabriele Jancke.

evidence.says: Yale's history prize essay records list Eric Robert Papenfuse's The Evils of Necessity: Robert Goodloe Harper and the Moral Dilemma of Slavery.
Yale's residential college seminar records list Eric Papenfuse for 1998–1999.
Cites Eric Robert Papenfuse's H-SHEAR review of The Natures of John and William Bartram, dated March 23, 1998.

basis: Yale's records associate the author of the work on a with Yale, and list Eric Papenfuse there in 1998–1999, matching the affiliation and year of b's review. The shared institution and dates support the identity, although the records do not directly link both works.

evidence.says: Gloria Chuku's CV lists Igbo Women and Economic Transformation (2005) and her 2006 H-Net review of Murder at Montpelier.

basis: Chuku's university-hosted CV lists a book on key a and the review on key b as her own publications.

evidence.says: Lists Roger A. Beaumont's 1973 Kansas State PhD dissertation, Military Elite Units in the Twentieth Century, and his 1974 book Military Elites.
Lists Military Elites and Special Operations and Elite Units, 1939–1988 under Roger A. Beaumont.

basis: The military history bibliography attributes the dissertation on key b and Military Elites on key a to the same author. The Texas A&M catalogue also groups that book with another work on key a.

evidence.says: Charles W. Humphries's Whitney biography says it grew out of his thesis, supervised by Maurice Careless.
A scholarly chapter cites Charles Humphries's PhD thesis, 'The Political Career of Sir James P. Whitney'.

basis: The book's preface identifies a thesis as its origin; a scholarly citation independently identifies Humphries's Whitney thesis by the title on the other key. The preface does not name the thesis, so the identification is inferred.

evidence.says: The 2023 review is by Clarence Y. H. Lo of the University of Missouri, with ORCID 0000-0002-2458-7382.
University of Missouri professor Clarence Y. H. Lo authored Small Property Versus Big Government and co-edited Social Policy and the Conservative Agenda.

basis: The review author and the author of both books share the same full name and University of Missouri affiliation. The university profile ties the book-side works to its professor, matching the review's affiliation and ORCID.

evidence.says: Benjamin Weber's 2009 Toulouse II doctorate became Lutter contre les Turcs, published in 2013; his CV lists appointments in France through 2015.
Benjamin Weber, an English professor at Wheaton since 2017, holds a Cornell PhD and lists A Brief History of Anglo-Saxon Education among his publications.
A brief history of Anglo-Saxon education is by Benjamin Weber of Wheaton College and was first published in 2018.
The 2016 Annales review of Philippe Buc's Holy War, Martyrdom, and Terror is credited to Benjamin Weber.

basis: The book author and the Wheaton article author have distinct doctoral training and careers. Key b appears mixed: its Annales review may belong to the book author, so that credit should be reviewed separately rather than merging the keys.

evidence.says: John Jay lists Charlotte Walker-Said's book Faith, Power and Family and her article Christian Marriage Between Tradition and Modernity.
The publisher credits the 2017 Christian Marriage article to Charlotte Walker-Said and gives ORCID 0000-0002-3305-537X.

basis: John Jay identifies the author of the article on key a as the author of the book on key b. The publisher also links the article directly to key a's ORCID.

evidence.says: Daniel Krebs's CV lists the 2005 report on Krieg und Migration in der Frühen Neuzeit and the 2013 book A Generous and Merciful Enemy.

basis: Krebs's university-hosted CV lists the conference report on the first key and the book on the second key under the same person.
